newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE sees non-oil sector driving 1997 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: UAE sees non-oil sector driving 1997 GDP growth.

text.p: Forecast 4.4 percent growth in nominal gross domestic product in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) this year was based mainly on growth in the non-oil sector, the economy minister said in remarks published on Tuesday.
"We estimate a 4.4 percent growth in GDP to 171 billion dirhams in 1997 from 163.7 billion dirhams in 1996," Minister of Economy and Commerce Sheikh Fahem bin Sultan al-Qassimi said.
"This will be the result of an increased contribution by the non-oil sector, together with the oil sector's contribution," he said in an interview with the daily al-Khaleej newspaper.

Qassimi, who took up his post after a March cabinet reshuffle, said the non-oil sector was expected to grow by about five percent in 1997. Preliminary figures show non-oil GDP at current prices expanded by 6.3 percent in 1996.
Like its Gulf Arab neighbours, the UAE wants to diversify its oil-dominated economy and boost the private sector's role.

He said the oil sector will remain a major contributor to the country's economy with forecast growth of 3.5 percent in 1997. Last year crude oil's contribution to nominal GDP shot up by more than 20 percent due to high world oil prices.
"We expect market demand for crude oil to continue accelerating, lifting prices and contributing effectively to GDP growth," Qassimi said.
Preliminary figures show GDP at current prices rose 10.9 percent in 1996.
